Check Long Incident Reports Before Subset Review

checkSubsetIncidents.Rd

Collect unmatched persons and classes, conflicting assignments, and unresolved block positions before reviewing incident reports. Class membership comes from the response data; no separate person-to-class table is needed.

Usage

checkSubsetIncidents(dat, incidents, booklets, blocks, rotation,
                     subunits = NULL, ID = "ID", classID = "classId",
                     dataLevel = c("subunit", "unit"))

# S3 method for class 'subsetIncidentCheck'
print(x, ..., max_problems = 0L)

Arguments

dat

A nonempty data frame of wide response data: one row per person and one column per response. Person IDs must be unique, nonmissing and nonblank. Unless classID = NULL, class IDs must also be nonmissing and nonblank. Response values may be NA.

incidents

A nonempty long data frame with columns named by ID and classID, plus blockPosition. With classID = NULL, the class column is not required. Each row reports one affected block position, a positive finite whole number such as 1 or 2; numeric values and their character equivalents are accepted. Optional level entries are "person" or "class". Optional issueId entries must be nonmissing and nonblank but may repeat; optional comment entries may be missing. Person IDs may be missing only for class reports; see Details for the all-supplied/all-missing rule and automatic level selection.

booklets

A data frame, normally inputList$booklets, with a unique booklet identifier and columns block1, block2, etc. Entries in these columns are block identifiers; NA and blank entries denote unoccupied positions. Positive integer column suffixes specify the positions, regardless of column order. Required; cannot be NULL.

blocks

A data frame, normally inputList$blocks, with subunit, block and subunitBlockPosition. Positions must be positive finite whole numbers (numeric or character equivalents). Subunits and positions must be unique within each relevant block. Required; cannot be NULL.

rotation

A data frame, normally inputList$rotation, with columns named by ID and booklet, with one row per relevant person. Missing booklet assignments are reported by the check. Required; cannot be NULL.

subunits

NULL (default) or a mapping data frame, normally inputList$subunits, with unique subunit, optional subunitRecoded, and unit. Required, including the unit column, with dataLevel = "unit"; otherwise optional. Names and assignments are identifiers, not response values. Supply the complete table from the same input list as the design tables. See prepareSubsetInfo.

ID

A single nonempty character string naming the person-ID column in response, incident and rotation data, e.g. "learner_key". Default: "ID". Supply a column name, not a vector of IDs. It must differ from classID and reserved incident/output names. Input columns do not need to be renamed.

classID

A single nonempty character string naming the class-ID column in response and incident data, e.g. "group_key", or NULL for individual data without classes. Default: "classId". It must differ from ID and reserved incident/output names. NULL forbids class-level reports.

dataLevel

A single character string: "subunit" (default) or "unit". "subunit" resolves original or recoded subunit columns; "unit" resolves aggregated units through subunits$unit. Supply the same level to prepareSubsetInfo.

x

A subsetIncidentCheck list returned by checkSubsetIncidents.

...

Additional print arguments; currently ignored.

max_problems

A single nonnegative whole number (numeric or integer), or Inf, giving the maximum number of problem details to print. NA, NULL, negative and fractional values are not allowed. The default 0 shows the case/response overview. Positive values additionally show counts by code and up to that many details; use Inf for all details. The returned problem table always contains all detected problems.

Details

Within each class, incident person IDs must be either all supplied or all missing. With supplied IDs, only the reported person–position pairs are selected. With all IDs missing, every reported position applies to every member of that class in dat. NA, empty strings and whitespace-only strings count as missing. Mixed missing and supplied person IDs within a class are errors, even if a supplied ID is absent from dat. Missing or contradictory class assignments are not inferred or repaired. Class IDs must identify classes uniquely across schools.

With classID = NULL, every incident needs a person ID and only level = "person" is allowed. A missing class column is not interpreted as an automatic request for this mode. When level is omitted, missing person IDs imply class reports and supplied IDs imply person reports. An explicit person report always needs a person ID; an explicit class report with supplied person IDs still selects only those persons.

issueId is optional: by default a unique identifier is generated per source row. Supplied identifiers must be nonmissing but may repeat across long rows of the same incident. Original row numbers are always retained separately as sourceRow. Repeated selections are permitted. Conflicting positions for a subunit response, or different units resolving to the same response, are reported. blockPosition must be a positive whole number and is resolved separately for each person's booklet.

The review scope is defined by dat and incidents. Input-list tables provide lookup information; this is not a comprehensive metadata audit. Only the reported persons, their booklets and the requested block positions are used for design validation. All members of selected units are retained when determining whether single-subunit aliases are allowed. Use checkInputList separately for input-list structure and its metadata consistency checks, and checkDesign for broader design/data checks.

The checker does not modify responses or open review menus. Missing required columns, duplicate keys in the relevant tables and other unusable structures raise errors immediately. Design resolution is attempted only after a row's identifiers and position are valid; dependent problems cannot be assessed until those inputs are corrected. One problem can affect several long rows, and one class row can produce problems for several persons.

All subunits in each resolved incident block are mapped to the selected response level, including when several columns are absent. Counts refer to the requested incident selections, not to every item in the design tables. In subunit mode, exactly one original or recoded column must exist. In unit mode, the unit-named column takes precedence. If it is absent, original or recoded subunit names are accepted only for units having exactly one subunit in the mapping table. Multiple candidate columns are ambiguous; a component column never substitutes for a multi-subunit aggregate. Absent response columns are omitted from the selection and recorded in ignored; their distinct identifiers remain in missing. Ambiguous columns remain unresolved_item problems.

In unit mode, any affected subunit selects the whole unit for that person. Several subunits or block positions can select the same unit, which is counted, displayed and recoded once. All originating subunit positions remain in the mapping. A design subunit without a unit assignment and without a direct match to a response column (original or known recoded name) is also omitted and recorded in ignored. No unit name is guessed. If a response column does match but the unit assignment is missing, missing_unit_mapping remains a problem. Supply the complete subunit mapping so that single-subunit units can be identified correctly.

A person with entirely missing responses is still present in dat. For items, an existing response column containing only NA is also present. For whole-class reports, membership is defined by dat; missing class members cannot be identified without an external roster or explicit incident person IDs. Numeric identifiers retain stored precision; import IDs as character to preserve leading zeros or digits beyond numeric precision.

Value

A subsetIncidentCheck list with:

summary

A one-row data frame. incidentRows counts source rows. matchedCaseRows counts rows with valid person/class assignments and report fields, independently of item/design resolution. absentCaseRows counts rows whose case findings only involve absent IDs; invalidCaseRows counts rows with other case/report-field findings. These three counts sum to incidentRows. Block-position validation belongs to the response check. readyRows counts incident rows with at least one selected response and no actionable problems. matchedRows is an alias for readyRows. problemRows counts rows with entries in problems; emptyRows counts rows without actionable problems but with no response to select. These three counts sum to incidentRows. A zero matchedRows does not mean that no persons were found in dat. problemPersons, problemClasses and problemItems count distinct nonmissing identifiers in the problem table, including existing persons affected by item problems and members of whole-class reports. missingPersons, missingClasses and missingItems count distinct identifiers actually absent from dat; repeated long rows or occurrences across persons do not inflate these totals. ambiguousItems counts distinct items with multiple candidate response columns. These item counts use the chosen dataLevel. missingSubunits and missingUnits give explicit totals: the inactive level is NA because it is not checked. unmappedSubunits counts relevant subunits requiring unit assignments in unit mode. ignoredRows, ignoredSubunits and ignoredUnits count distinct identifiers in ignored, excluding NA. Ignored rows can also have available responses and therefore overlap with readyRows. uncheckedItemRows counts source rows whose item checks could not be completed for at least one person because of invalid identifiers, positions or unresolved design, including absent cases. pendingItemRows restricts incomplete checks to rows counted in matchedCaseRows. checkedItems counts distinct logical identifiers whose response columns were assessed (matched, missing or ambiguous); unmapped subunits are excluded. itemCheckComplete is true when there are matched cases and neither pending item checks nor invalid case/report fields remain. Absent cases alone do not make the response check incomplete. This flag describes coverage within the available-data review scope, not completeness of the input-list metadata. Ignored design entries do not make it false; ambiguities affecting existing responses still prevent preparation. A zero missing-item count is only the number detected so far when this flag is false. Class counts are zero with classID = NULL.

problems

A data frame with sourceRow, issueId, the person ID, blockPosition, code, message, item, itemStatus, booklet, block, subunit, subunitRecoded, unit, datCols, mappingIssue, and, when used, the class ID. ID columns use the names supplied in ID and classID. It has zero rows when there are no actionable findings; omitted design entries are reported separately in ignored. subunit retains the original design identifier, unit its aggregation target, and datCols the uniquely resolved response column (NA if unresolved). item is retained as a level-dependent identifier: the subunit in subunit mode, the unit in unit mode. itemStatus is "ambiguous" or "unmapped" for item problems. mappingIssue distinguishes "subunit_not_listed" from "unit_not_assigned" (an empty unit assignment). Inapplicable or unknown details are NA.

byCode

A data frame with one row per problem code: problems counts problem records; incidentRows, persons, classes, items, subunits and units count distinct nonmissing identifiers within that code. Subunit/unit counts here describe affected identifiers, not necessarily absent response columns. These counts must not be summed across codes to obtain overall totals because the same identifier may occur under several codes.

missing

A list of character vectors persons, classes, subunits, units and items, containing the distinct identifiers absent from dat. items is an alias for the active level's vector. Original and recoded aliases count as one logical response. The inactive level's vector is empty; consult dataLevel or the NA count in summary.

dataLevel

The response level used for this check.

mapping

A data frame recording each subunit in the incident selections whose block design could be resolved, including successful mappings and item problems. It contains source rows, person/class IDs, booklet and block positions, subunit, subunitRecoded, unit, item, datCols, itemStatus, mappingIssue and ignoredReason. Successful mappings have status "matched". Several rows may refer to one unit response. Rows blocked by invalid incident identifiers or unavailable design do not appear here.

mappingIssues

A deduplicated data frame of actionable subunit-to-unit assignments with subunit, subunitRecoded, unit and mappingIssue. It distinguishes design subunits absent from subunits$subunit from listed subunits with missing/empty subunits$unit. These are assignment findings, not evidence that the response data lack those units.

ignored

The subset of mapping omitted from the review, with ignoredReason equal to "response_column_absent" or "unmapped_without_data_match". The latter records a missing unit assignment without a matching original/recoded response column; it makes no claim about the presence of an unknown unit. These rows do not block preparation. Entries in unrelated blocks or for unreported persons are outside the check altogether.

Problem codes include unknown_person, unknown_class, class_mismatch, mixed_person_ids, missing_person_id, missing_class_id, class_without_id, missing_issue_id, invalid_level, invalid_position, unknown_booklet, unknown_block, not_administered, unresolved_item, missing_unit_mapping, and ambiguous_cell. Printing separates case matching from response-column resolution. Missing-column counts are labelled as partial when coverage is incomplete, or as not yet assessed when no logical response could be checked. Repeated problem records and counts by code are available on request via max_problems; full details always remain in the returned data frames.

See also

prepareSubsetInfo, visualSubsetRecode, vignette("subset_review", package = "eatPrep")

Examples

dat <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2"), classId = "K1", I1 = c(1, NA))
booklets <- data.frame(booklet = "X", block1 = "A")
blocks <- data.frame(subunit = "I1", block = "A", subunitBlockPosition = 1)
rotation <- data.frame(ID = dat$ID, booklet = "X")
incidents <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "absent"), classId = "K1", blockPosition = 1)
checked <- checkSubsetIncidents(dat, incidents, booklets, blocks, rotation)
checked
#> Incident check (subunit responses)
#> Cases: 1 of 2 incident rows matched to dat.
#> Absent from dat: 1 persons, 0 classes (1 incident rows).
#> Missing subunit columns: 0 detected among 1 distinct subunit identifiers checked.
#> Ready for review: 1 incident rows.
#> Details: x$byCode, x$problems, or print(x, max_problems = 10).
checked$summary[c("missingPersons", "missingItems", "missingClasses")]
#>   missingPersons missingItems missingClasses
#> 1              1            0              0
checked$missing
#> $persons
#> [1] "absent"
#> 
#> $classes
#> character(0)
#> 
#> $items
#> character(0)
#> 
#> $subunits
#> character(0)
#> 
#> $units
#> character(0)
#> 
checked$byCode
#>             code problems incidentRows persons classes items subunits units
#> 1 unknown_person        1            1       1       1     0        0     0
checked$problems
#>   sourceRow issueId     ID blockPosition           code
#> 1         2    row2 absent             1 unknown_person
#>                      message item itemStatus booklet block subunit
#> 1 Person is absent from dat. <NA>       <NA>    <NA>  <NA>    <NA>
#>   subunitRecoded unit datCols mappingIssue classId
#> 1           <NA> <NA>    <NA>         <NA>      K1
